and certain local officials relating to certain construction and other

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4013

SPONSOR: COMRIE
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the administrative code of the city of New York and the
public authorities law, in relation to requiring notice to members of
the legislature and certain local officials relating to certain
construction and other projects affecting such members' and officials'
districts

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This purpose of this bill is to ensure that elected officials are better
informed of construction projects in New York City.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

This bill would expand:

-the delivery of:

*notifications on major transportation projects .in New York City to
include State assembly members and senators and enable such State offi-
cials to submit recommendations and/or comments within ten business days
after the receipt of such major transportation project notices;

*notifications on temporary closing of streets in New York City to
include State assembly members and senators and enable such State offi-
cials to submit issues raised at public forums on fully closed streets;

*notifications on pedestrian plaza designations in New York City to
include State assembly members and senators;

*notifications on work affecting a street segment or intersection that
has a bike lane in New York City to include State assembly members and
senators;

*maps or plans from the New York City Department of Environmental
Protection (DEP) to include City Council members, State assembly members
and senators;

*raising grade drainage plans from the New York City DEP to include
assembly members and senators; City Council members, State assembly
members and senators;

*copies of documents on the construction of sewers by the owners of
private property from the New York City DEP to include City Council
members, State assembly members and senators;

*construction projects plans from the New York City School Construction

*copies of documents on the construction of sewers by the owners of
Authority to include City Council members, State assembly members and
senators;

*citizen participation for local brownfield work from the New York City
DEP to include City Council members, State assembly members and
senators;
*notice requirements for public utility companies to include the name
and contact information of the permittee(s), the anticipated start and
end dates of the work, the location, nature and extent of the work to be
performed, and the permit type; and,

*notice requirements for filming permits to include the name and contact
information of the permittee(s), the anticipated start and end dates of
the production, and the location, nature and extent of the production.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Notifications for construction projects in New York City, such as NYC
Department of Environmental Protection water main and sewer replace-
ments, or the acquisition of property by the NYC School Construction
Authority, are currently sent to City Council members, community boards
and borough presidents. State elected officials are often not informed
about these plans, or the issuance of film permits in their district.
Since the implications of these projects affect the constituents of not
only City officials, but elected State officials as well, the delivery
of notifications should be expanded to include elected State officials
so that they are better able to address the concerns of their constitu-
ents.

Additionally, there is no requirement that utilities notify elected
officials about long-term repair projects. This bill would ensure that
both City and State representatives are updated about work by utilities
such as Con Edison and National Grid.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is new legislation.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
